discussion_comments.comment_body:
**[MAJOR] Fragment idempotency: upgrades never land, same-key fragments silently drop, cross-plugin order is load order.**

- this sentinel encodes no version or content hash, so a plugin upgrade that rewrites a fragment's prose is filtered as already-present forever, with no drop record
- two fragments sharing (bundle, anchor, order) silently drop the second; 10-authoring-a-plugin.md line 170 promises "a build error", and no such validation exists in package.ts or compose.ts
- for after-step anchors, insertion is "before the next `^#{2,3}` heading", and a previously spliced fragment's own `###` heading becomes that boundary, so a later plugin's fragment splices BEFORE an earlier plugin's regardless of order (simulated on the real build-and-test body: order 200 lands before order 100). Since each plugin runs its own hook, the documented "(order, bundle), never by load order" interleave (18-plugin-mechanism.md lines 135, 176) is in practice reverse hook-firing order.

Suggest: include a content hash in the marker (upgrade = replace the block), add the promised same-key build error at package time, and make the splice skip past already-spliced plugin blocks when locating the anchor boundary (or re-derive the anchor region from desired state each run).

Fixed in `7c00c7f`. Sentinels now carry a content hash (`<!-- plugin:bundle:anchor:order:hash -->` + a matching close marker). (a) An upgraded fragment (changed prose → changed hash) replaces its prior block instead of being filtered as present-forever. (b) A same-(bundle,anchor,order) collision within a contribution is dropped-with-log. (c) Insertion no longer keys on "the next heading": blocks are self-delimiting, so a new fragment is placed at its ordered (order,bundle) slot among existing peer blocks. Verified a 2nd plugin composing order-95 in a separate hook run lands BEFORE test-pro's already-present order-100 block.

discussion_comments.comment_body: This collects every `SWARM_UNIT_CONVERGED` row in the intent, keyed only on `Unit name`. The row (emitUnitConverged, aidlc-swarm.ts:259) carries just `Batch number` + `Unit name` — no stage/Bolt id — and the audit is append-only. So if the same per-unit construction stage re-runs with the same unit names (recompose / re-entry), the prior run's converged rows make the fresh batch look already-built and it gets skipped. If a per-unit stage can re-run in the current flow, scope this set to the current stage run (a stage id on the event, or a timestamp floor). If it genuinely can't re-run, a comment saying so would settle it.
